title: Async Streaming Pipeline with Backpressure & Batching
problemStatement: Implement `async function* batchAsyncStream(asyncIterable, batchSize)` that reads from an async iterable source and yields arrays of items chunked by `batchSize`. Any remaining items when the stream closes must be yielded in a final partial batch.
interviewTrap: Failing to handle trailing remaining items when an async iterator completes causes silent data loss. Consuming without backpressure risks memory ballooning.

testCases.name: Chunks stream into equal batches
testCases.testFn: async function* src() { yield 1; yield 2; yield 3; yield 4; } const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

testCases.name: Flushes remaining items on stream completion
testCases.testFn: async function* src() { yield 1; yield 2; yield 3; yield 4; yield 5; } const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

testCases.name: Yields nothing for empty stream
testCases.testFn: async function* src() {} const res = []; for await (const b of batchAsyncStream(src(), 2)) res.push(b); return res;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Generators are re-entrant state machines. When yield is encountered, the generator's execution context is suspended and pushed out of the call stack. Calling .next() re-attaches the context and resumes evaluation.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Async Generators & Flow Control Backpressure.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Async Generators & Flow Control Backpressure is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Failing to handle trailing remaining items when an async iterator completes causes silent data loss. Consuming without backpressure risks memory ballooning.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does an Async Generator pipeline implement streaming backpressure?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: An async generator does not pull or yield the next item until the consumer explicitly awaits `.next()`. If a consumer is slow (e.g. slow database writes), the upstream generator remains suspended at `yield`, pausing data reads from the source socket.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests deep systems understanding of stream flow control.

realWorldUseCases.description: Exporting 5 million database rows to S3: query generator pulls 1,000 rows, transforms them, and streams to S3 multipart upload with bounded memory.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: for await (const chunk of etlPipeline(dbStream)) { await s3.write(chunk); }

howToExplain.opening: Async generator pipelines combine streaming transformation stages with automatic backpressure, keeping memory bounded regardless of dataset scale.
keyPoints: Naturally throttles upstream data generation to consumer speed.
Handles batching, filtering, and asynchronous mapping cleanly.
The standard pattern for modern stream processing in Node.js 18+.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Async streaming pipelines prevent memory exhaustion when processing datasets larger than available RAM.
analogies: A bucket brigade fighting a fire: nobody passes a bucket until the person in front is ready to catch it.

commonMistakes.mistake: Loading entire dataset into memory before starting pipeline.
commonMistakes.why: Defeats the entire purpose of streaming, risking Out-Of-Memory crashes.
commonMistakes.correct: Stream item by item or in small fixed batches.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does Node.js stream.pipeline() integrate with Async Generators?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Node.js `stream.pipeline` natively accepts async generators as pipeline stages: `pipeline(sourceStream, async function* (source) { ... }, destStream)`.
